title: 2026-09-08 POC Weekly - Latency Tuning (Novapay)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on latency tuning. Reviewed latest TTFT and p95 numbers after kernel and streaming changes; validated KV cache hit pattern; discussed streaming chunk size and sequence length tradeoffs. Agreed to run two benchmark variants (2k seq vs 512 seq) with triton kernels + 4-bit quantization and share telemetry logs. Next call scheduled in one week.
topics: kernel selection: cuBLAS vs Triton vs custom kernels
KV cache behavior and prefix caching
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, 2pm PT. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Lena Ortiz: Hey, Lena here.
[00:07] Marcus Li: Marcus, SRE.
[00:09] Priya Sharma: Priya, ML.
[00:11] Ethan Nguyen: Ethan, infra.
[00:13] Sanjay Rao: Sanjay from Redwood SE. Jamie, you wanna kick off?
[00:18] Jamie Park: Yeah, thanks. Real quick agenda: quick perf recap, what we changed last week — kernel flags and streaming chunking — show numbers, then plan the benchmark runs.
[00:28] Sanjay Rao: Quick context: last Thursday we pushed the triton kernel experiment on the dedicated pool and also toggled continuous prefix KV cache for the 512-seq baseline.
[00:36] Priya Sharma: I saw the dashboard — TTFT was lower but p95 still spiky.
[00:40] Jamie Park: Right. Baseline week before was TTFT ~220ms median and p95 ~360ms on your representative prompts. After kernel swap + cache we got median 165ms and p95 ~270ms on the 512 sequence set — numbers are from the test harness we ran yesterday.
[00:54] Marcus Li: Where are those measurements captured? Is that from your internal telemetry or our agent?
[00:58] Sanjay Rao: Both — we pulled Redwood tracing logs plus your exported harness. We'll share the CSV and the flamegraphs. There may be small clock skew but overall pattern holds.
[01:08] Ethan Nguyen: Cool. I noticed CPU spin on the host when streaming was on, any link?
[01:12] Sanjay Rao: Yeah, that's likely from the streaming chunk assembly on the host. We currently assemble 64-token chunks by default which reduces RTTs for some prompts but adds host-side CPU cost when many small requests stream concurrently.
[01:24] Lena Ortiz: Hmm, our workload is a high qps of short prompts — so TTFT really matters. We care less about larger seqs for now but still need p95 under 300ms.
[01:33] Jamie Park: Noted. So two levers: reduce chunk size to 16–32 tokens to favor TTFT, and tune kernel selection for small-batch low-latency paths.
[01:42] Priya Sharma: Any tradeoffs for quality when we push 4-bit quant?
[01:45] Sanjay Rao: We saw negligible regression on the eval set for the smaller conversation prompts, but longer context generation (2k tokens) shows some deg of degradation for certain rare tokens. We'll include quality smoke tests.
[01:56] Marcus Li: On the kernel front, can you explain cuBLAS vs Triton tradeoff? We've seen cuBLAS stable but higher TTFT?
[02:03] Sanjay Rao: Sure. cuBLAS kernels are well tuned for throughput but have higher kernel launch overhead for short sequences and tiny batches; Triton kernels have lower launch overhead with custom fused attention and better small-batch performance. There's also an internal custom fused attention path we tested that helps for seq < 256.
[02:18] Jamie Park: Important note: when you use continuous KV cache we reduce repeated attention compute but prefix cache increases memory working set. For your 512 baseline it helped a lot; for 2k it could cause memory pressure unless we pin to dedicated pool with bigger GPU memory.
[02:34] Priya Sharma: That explains some of the OOM spikes we saw.
[02:37] Ethan Nguyen: Right, we hit one OOM on a 2k seq run last week on a 48GB instance.
[02:42] Sanjay Rao: That's expected. For 2k sequences we recommend either multi-GPU sharding or model-variant with 4-bit quant + offloaded KV.
[02:51] Lena Ortiz: Let's talk concrete next steps — what do you want us to run on our side?
[02:55] Jamie Park: Two benchmark variants: (A) low-latency optimized: 512 seq, chunk size 16, Triton kernels, 4-bit quant on the model, continuous KV cache on; (B) long-context validation: 2k seq, chunk 64, cuBLAS or fused attention, 4-bit with offloaded KV, smaller batch sizes. We'll provide a perf harness config.
[03:17] Priya Sharma: How long will each run take?
[03:20] Sanjay Rao: Each run ~2–3 hours for stable stats at 95th percentile. If you want quicker smoke, we can do 30min runs but p95 will be noisy.
[03:28] Marcus Li: Are you able to run the triton kernel on our Dedicated nodes without downtime?
[03:32] Jamie Park: Yes, it's a config toggle — we can flip per-pool. We'll coordinate a brief maintenance window but it should be seamless.
[03:39] Ethan Nguyen: Any risks to data or config?
[03:41] Sanjay Rao: No data risk. It's a runtime flag; we keep prior kernel builds ready to roll back. We'll also snapshot the pool.
[03:47] Lena Ortiz: Can you also surface the per-operation timing breakdown? We need per-token vs first-byte vs host-assembly.
[03:53] Sanjay Rao: Yep, we'll export the trace with breakdown: socket->gpu transfer, kernel exec, decode time, host assembly.
[03:59] Jamie Park: I'll send the perf spreadsheet and the harness config after the call.
[04:03] Priya Sharma: About streaming, you mentioned chunk assembly; will smaller chunk sizes hurt throughput?
[04:08] Sanjay Rao: It can increase total tokens processed per second due to overhead, but for your low-latency critical workload it's a net win — you trade some throughput for lower TTFT and p50/p90.
[04:18] Marcus Li: On quant: what profile did you use? We need to know which ops were per-channel vs per-tensor.
[04:23] Sanjay Rao: We used a mixed profile: most matmuls per-channel, activations per-tensor, and we kept softmax in fp16. We'll include the quant config.
[04:31] Lena Ortiz: Any expected cost delta? If TTFT improves but throughput drops, cost per token might increase.
[04:36] Jamie Park: Good question. Our back-of-envelope: the low-latency config increases CPU host cost by about 8–12% but reduces user-facing timeouts and support costs. We also expect token compute cost to be similar due to quant. We'll attach estimated cost delta in the spreadsheet.
[04:48] Priya Sharma: Can you also test with streaming disabled so we have apples-to-apples?
[04:51] Sanjay Rao: Yes, we'll run A' and B' variants with streaming off.
[04:55] Ethan Nguyen: For the 48GB issues, want us to provision a 80GB node for the 2k run?
[04:59] Jamie Park: That would be helpful, if available. If not, we can shard.
[05:03] Lena Ortiz: Alright, recap and owners?
[05:06] Jamie Park: Recap: Redwood to share perf CSV, traces, and harness config (owner: Jamie). Redwood to schedule kernel toggle and run internal validations (owner: Sanjay). Novapay to run two benchmark variants and share logs (owner: Priya/Marcus). We'll reconvene next Tuesday same time.
[05:20] Marcus Li: One more Q: Any recommended model variant? We were using rwd-open-3b-v1 (I think).
[05:25] Sanjay Rao: rwd-open-3b-v1 is fine; for long-context we have rwd-open-3b-long that has attention tweaks. We'll recommend that for the 2k test.
[05:33] Priya Sharma: Great. Also add a quick quality smoke: 50 human prompts check for hallucination rate on 2k contexts.
[05:39] Jamie Park: Yes, include that.
[05:41] Lena Ortiz: Thanks, everyone.
[05:43] Jamie Park: Thanks all. We'll follow up with artifacts and schedule.
[05:47] [END TRANSCRIPT]
